newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower in quiet trading on Monday as market players remained cautious ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Not even news of a fall in German M3 money supply growth in June could halt the decline in debt prices, which traded in a narrow band for much of the day.
"It's been a quiet day with guilders trading in line with Bunds," one dealer said.
Greenspan, whose public comments are usually keenly awaited by financial markets, will deliver his semi-annual Humphrey Hawkins economic report to the U.S. Congress on Tuesday.
"People are pretty neutral. There's little room for a big change in policy," another dealer said of the market's outlook for U.S. interest rates.
"But it's important to see what his stand will be for the next month."
The Bundesbank earlier announced that M3 grew at an annualised rate of 6.4 percent in June from 7.0 percent in May.
Dealers reported some cash activity in Dutch bonds, with buyers targetting maturities up to 2005 on price weakness.
"Every time the market dips, you see customers coming in to pick up some paper," a trader said.
